To describe the architecture of the Flight Booking System, the following views are presented:
This view presents the system's modular decomposition into functional components and subsystems.
User Service: Handles authentication, registration, account management.
Flight Service: Manages flight schedules, availability, and airline data.
Booking Service: Manages reservation logic, seat selection, baggage options.
Payment Service: Interfaces with third-party gateways (e.g., VNPay, MoMo), processes transactions.
Notification Service: Sends email/SMS for confirmations and alerts.
Admin Service: Enables airline staff and admins to manage flights, bookings, and users.
Gateway API: Serves as the entry point, performs routing, rate limiting, and JWT validation.
This view outlines the organization of code and deployment artifacts.
Each subsystem is implemented as an independent microservice (Node.js or Spring Boot).
Shared libraries for logging, validation, and security are maintained in a common module.
CI/CD pipelines are configured for each service separately.
Message Broker: Redis Pub/Sub for async messaging
Describes the physical deployment of system components.
Hosted on a cloud provider (e.g., AWS, GCP, or Azure)
Database Nodes: PostgreSQL primary + replicas, MongoDB
Redis Cluster: For caching and Pub/Sub
Region: Singapore (Low latency for local users)
Services are containerized using Docker and orchestrated via Kubernetes
Focuses on data models and storage strategy.
PostgreSQL: Relational storage for users, bookings, transactions
MongoDB: For flexible flight data and logs
Redis: Short-lived data (e.g., OTP, session tokens, pending verification)
All sensitive data encrypted at rest
HTTPS enforced in all client-server and inter-service communication
Role-based access for each database cluster node
